verdict.rationale: The evidence shows PagerDuty has schedules, mobile schedule views, a Shift Agent that monitors calendars for conflicts, and a REST API to find out who is on call. None of it documents a subscribable calendar feed (e.g. iCal/webcal) that syncs a user's shifts to a personal calendar. The Shift Agent reads calendars to coordinate swaps, which is an adjacent feature, and the REST API is only a developer building block, so neither earns credit for this story.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, my shifts sync to my personal calendar via a feed so I always know when I'm on the hook
